kind: One run at full size and full length, one seed: the lifted loop with power-law cells if the bed's four-seed reading holds, else fsp-lift's second seed; trained and scored as fsp-lift, beside fsp-lift and v19's pair.
why: fsp-lift (full_size_lifted_loop_run.json) runs in the form its pilots picked: two passes, a budget of 507,000, 6e-4, the pool that lifts the ceiling (fll-decide: a third pass 0.0008 better, the Transformer's rate 0.0031 better, neither 0.005). Of the changes piloted at full size beside it after 24,000 updates against fs-loop6-lift (1.300729), one passed: power-law cells (--granule-power 8), 0.0137 better [-0.0145, -0.0129] at equal parameters and 0.4% more pulses (full_size_power_cells.json). The others stay out: twice the budget 0.0005 worse (full_size_loop_budget.json), weight decay on synapses only 0.0017 worse (full_size_decay_synapses_only.json), energy pools 0.0040 worse (energy_pool.json); loop phases failed on the bed (loop_phases_with_data.json). By power_cells_with_data.json's amendment, power-law cells join the next full-length run only if the bed's four-seed reading (seeds 20001 to 20004 at 24,000 updates, --min-wins 3) is a fix or a constant gain as well; that reading lands tonight, after this record. If it fails, nothing passed, and the run is fsp-lift's second seed, which gives the spread of full-length runs that every comparison at this length has lacked. The code copy of f876392 scores fs-loop6-lift's weights bit for bit as fsp-lift's copy of 97a2772 does (8,000 validation bytes as 4 streams on the server's CPU), so the pilot's pair does not mix in a change of code.

arm.fsp-lift2: If the four-seed reading is a fix or a constant gain: CODE=v18c sched/bin/full-pair3.sh stack fsp-lift2 6e-4 --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 --pool-lifts-ceiling --granule-power 8, the flags in both stages, seed 20001 (fsp-lift's), on the code copy of f876392 that trained the full-size pilot. Otherwise fsp-lift's second seed: fsp-lift's flags without --granule-power on fsp-lift's code copy (v17n, 97a2772) with seed 20002, through a copy of full-pair3.sh that takes the seed from SEED (full-pair3.sh fixes 20001 and is not edited while fsp-lift runs it). Either way 36,263,956 parameters in the long stage: power-law cells add none.

training: Server GPU 0, alone (MPS=0), priority 5, GPU_MEM 85, queued after tonight's window closes so that it starts first when the window of Thursday 2026-11-26 opens at 16:45 UTC, and runs through the weekend's window by pause and resume; fsp-loop took 16.3 hours of training and about 1.5 of scoring. The bed work left on GPU 0 waits until it is done.
base: fsp-lift (scored in Thursday's window), fsp-loop, fsp-st and fsp-tf: the same data, schedule and scoring, and with power-law cells the same seed as fsp-lift.
measure: As full_size_lifted_loop_run.json: the full enwik8 test and validation splits as streams at the reach chosen on the first 1,000,000 validation bytes (the trained 2,048 or 8,192), with fast output synapses at 2^24 on the cells of every pass and without, paired piece by piece with fsp-lift, fsp-loop and fsp-tf (experiments/compare_stream_scores.py) and split by context (experiments/gap_by_piece.py, near 2,032, far 8,192); the pulses a byte, the training time and the share of membrane entries at their bound (experiments/membrane_saturation.py). With power-law cells also the cells' firing beside fsp-lift's (experiments/cell_activity.py on the first 8,192 validation bytes, lead 256, piece 256).
reading: (1) It beats the Transformer if its taught test score is below fsp-tf's frozen score with the paired 95% interval of the gap below zero, and the same holds on validation; the gap to fsp-tf with fast output synapses at 0.07 is recorded beside, the claim is made without reservation only if it holds against that too, and every claim states the pulses a byte. (2) With power-law cells: they improve the lifted loop at full length if fsp-lift2 is at least 0.005 better than fsp-lift on taught test and on taught validation, each interval clear of zero; within 0.003 on either split they do not, and between it is unclear. As fsp-lift's second seed: the two seeds' differences on both splits with their intervals are the spread, and no claim of a change is made. (3) If (2) holds, fsp-lift2's form is the stack's recipe from here on; otherwise the better-scored of the two seeds is reported and fsp-lift's form stays.
seen_before_recording: power_cells_screen.json (the laptop's seed: 0.0262 ahead at 6,000 updates, 0.0045 at 24,000), power_cells_with_data.json's result_two_seeds (a constant gain, 0.0128 on the mean at 24,000) and full_size_power_cells.json's result with the cells' firing; the other full-size pilots and bed screens named above; fsp-lift's training to update 63,000 (its in-training estimates only, not scored). Of seeds 3 and 4: the bases bed24-lr12-g3 and -g4 are trained and scored but not read; pw8-24k-g3 and -g4 are training, and the scheduler's status line showed their in-training estimates (1.6052 at update 21,000 and 1.8389 at 6,750), not paired with anything; pw8-6k-g3, pw8-6k-g4, rd-base-6k-g3 and rd-base-6k-g4 have not trained. The four-seed reading has not been computed.

decision.four_seed_reading: a constant gain (power_cells_with_data.json result_four_seeds): 24,000-update leads 0.0100, 0.0156, 0.0100, 0.0143, mean 0.0125, four seeds ahead; 6,000-update mean 0.0176
decision.arm: fsp-lift2 with power-law cells: CODE=v18c sched/bin/full-pair3.sh stack fsp-lift2 6e-4 --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 --pool-lifts-ceiling --granule-power 8, seed 20001
decision.queued: held on GPU 0 at priority 5, alone, GPU_MEM 85, right after this decision; released after tonight's window closes, so that it starts first at 16:45 UTC on 2026-11-26

result.run: fsp-lift2 as the decision named it (power-law cells, seed 20001): CODE=v18c sched/bin/full-pair3.sh stack fsp-lift2 6e-4 --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 --pool-lifts-ceiling --granule-power 8 on the server's GPU 0 alone (MPS=0), from the window of 2026-11-26 at 16:45 UTC; paused at the window's close at update 77,550 and resumed at 16:45 UTC on 2026-11-27; training ended at 19:41 UTC and the scoring at 20:59 UTC. 36,263,956 parameters, as fsp-lift.
result.reach: chosen on the first 1,000,000 validation bytes: 1.13271 at 8,192 against 1.14825 at the trained 2,048 (fsp-lift: 1.14015 and 1.15614), so 8,192
result.pairing: experiments/compare_stream_scores.py and experiments/gap_by_piece.py, run on the laptop on the bits of every piece copied from the server's scores, as for full_size_lifted_loop_run.json.
result.pulses a byte: fsp-lift2 511,954 in training and 506,607 on the trainer's validation streams, against fsp-lift's 511,340 and 506,746: the same budget of 507,000, spent alike within 0.1%.
result.training time: 59,238 s on the trainer's clock against fsp-lift's 58,820 s: the power-law cells cost 0.7%.

reading.(1): By the registered measure fsp-lift2 does not beat the Transformer: with fast output synapses it is 0.0055 behind fsp-tf's frozen score on test (0.0044 to 0.0066) and 0.0121 on validation (0.0110 to 0.0133), at 506,607 pulses a byte.
reading.(2): By the registered measure power-law cells do not improve the lifted loop; they make it worse: with fast output synapses fsp-lift2 is 0.0027 worse than fsp-lift on test (0.0022 to 0.0033) and 0.0034 on validation (0.0028 to 0.0040), each interval clear of zero.
reading.(3): (2) does not hold, so by the letter fsp-lift's form stays the stack's recipe and fsp-lift stays the best-scored spiking model on the registered measure (1.08175 test, 1.11358 validation).
reading.the fast output synapses (reported, not: The loss is the fast output synapses'. Read at 2^24 on all 18 passes, as every full-size stack since v19 was, they cost fsp-lift2 0.0092 on test (0.0088 to 0.0097) and 0.0115 on validation (0.0111 to 0.0119), where on fsp-lift they added 0.0009 on test and cost 0.0007 on validation. They still help copies (0.0445 on near copies and 0.0231 on far ones on test) and cost new contexts 0.0262 on test and 0.0283 on validation. The threshold of 2^24 was kept by a scan on fsp-loop (fast_synapse_threshold_loop.json), a stack of plain cells; no scan has been made with power-law cells.
reading.without fast output synapses (reported,: Read at the reach of 8,192 without fast output synapses, as full_size_lifted_loop_run.json reported fsp-lift beside its reading, fsp-lift2 scores 1.07524 on test and 1.10540 on validation. Power-law cells are then 0.0074 better than plain ones on both splits (0.0069 to 0.0080 each), and 0.0081 and 0.0083 better as trained (reach 2,048), more than the reading's mark of 0.005: the gain on the bed and in the pilots carried to full length, mostly on new contexts (0.0097 on test, 0.0140 on validation). Against the Transformer, both models then without fast synapses, fsp-lift2 is 0.0038 ahead on test (0.0027 to 0.0047 ahead) and 0.0006 behind on validation (0.0004 ahead to 0.0016 behind); against the Transformer with its fast synapses at 0.07, 0.0019 ahead on test and 0.0010 behind on validation (0.0001 to 0.0019). On new contexts the distance to the Transformer falls to 0.0262 on test and 0.0293 on validation (fsp-lift: 0.0439 and 0.0524), and on copies the stack stays far ahead (0.058 near and 0.425 far on test). This is not the registered measure, and a measure chosen after the scores were seen decides nothing: by these numbers fsp-lift2 would beat the Transformer on test and stand level with it on validation, which (1) would not count as beating it even on this measure. The first million validation bytes, read without fast synapses at the reach of 8,192, had shown the same 0.0074 (1.13271 against fsp-lift's 1.14015).
reading.firing (reported): With power-law cells 0.50 to 0.72 times as many cells fire at a byte at every level (0.032 to 0.234 of the cells, fsp-lift 0.052 to 0.384), a firing cell sends a longer tail of spikes (90th percentile 21 to 128 against 15 to 42), the levels send 20,675 cell spikes a byte against 18,331, and 22 cells never fire (fsp-lift none). Saturation stays negligible: 0.000001% of the cells' entries at their cap (fsp-lift 0.002%), 0.010% of the reads' (0.008%); the other populations stand at 6.7% (fsp-lift 2.9%).
reading.spread: One seed each, the same seed for fsp-lift and fsp-lift2: the full-size stack has no second seed, so how far two seeds of one recipe lie apart at full size is not known.

result.what follows: By the registered reading fsp-lift's form stays the recipe. What the untaught scores show is registered before it is claimed: full_size_power_cells_second_seed.json trains a second seed of fsp-lift2's recipe (seed 20002, on the fast training path after a check that the fast code scores fsp-lift2 to the same bits) and fixes in advance that both models are read without fast output synapses, the stack at the reach chosen on the first million validation bytes as before. The data-slope runs (full_size_data_slope.json) keep fsp-lift2's recipe as registered, scored with and without fast output synapses as every full-size stack is.
